items.title: Narvin Kimball Interview, 1961-11-25
items.q: Red Allen and I went to school. He was my upperclassman, though.

ctx.x: But your father worked with them then? Yes, he worked with them. And, uh, and, uh, well, you, uh, I interrupted you were going to tell about your first instrument and all your guitar and the band.

Well, I made that, I made that, uh, supposedly ukulele or banjo, whatever it was, and cut a hole in it, and would play with that. And, uh, I was in high school. And, uh, when I was in high school, later on when I went to high school, I, uh, I bought a ukulele. I had a little job in the afternoons after school. And, uh, I saved my money until I had about seven dollars and I bought a ukulele. Uh-huh. And brought it home on a Friday evening. Uh, Red Allen and I went to school. He was my upperclassman, though. And,…

No, he was at McDonald's 35 then. He was the only in high school. Yeah. And, uh, he played the ukulele very well. And, uh, I liked the way he played it. And, uh, it developed quite a bit of popularity for him being a ukulele player.
